title: HILP: Accounting for Workload-Level Parallelism in System-on-Chip Design Space Exploration
problem: Early-stage heterogeneous SoC design space exploration tools (MultiAmdahl, Gables) only model minimum and maximum workload-level parallelism (WLP) extremes; they cannot model realistic mixed-application workloads where multiple independent multi-phase applications share an SoC's heterogeneous cores and accelerators.
method: HILP formulates SoC workload scheduling as a job-shop scheduling problem: a set of independent multi-phase applications with phase-level dependencies is to be scheduled across heterogeneous cores and accelerators. This is solved using an integer linear programming (ILP) solver to find a near-optimal schedule that minimizes total workload execution time subject to power and memory bandwidth constraints. The ILP captures the full continuum of WLP (not just extremes) and can be used to sweep large design spaces efficiently during early exploration.

title: ReVeil: Unconstrained Concealed Backdoor Attack on Deep Neural Networks using Machine Unlearning
problem: Existing concealed backdoor attacks on DNNs require white-box/black-box model access or auxiliary data; this work targets data collection phase without model access.
method: ReVeil embeds backdoors during data collection phase of training without requiring model or auxiliary data access. It maintains low pre-deployment attack success rate through data poisoning, then restores high ASR via machine unlearning.

title: EDM: An Ultra-Low Latency Ethernet Fabric for Memory Disaggregation
problem: Achieving low remote memory access latency over Ethernet for memory disaggregation remains unsolved; existing protocols (TCP/IP, RDMA/RoCEv2) are implemented atop the Ethernet MAC layer and incur fundamental MAC-layer latency and bandwidth overheads that are particularly severe for small memory messages.
method: EDM implements the entire remote memory access protocol stack within the Physical layer (PHY) of the Ethernet, bypassing the MAC layer entirely to eliminate its fundamental latency overheads. At the switch level, EDM implements a centralized in-network scheduler operating within the Ethernet PHY, inspired by the Parallel Iterative Matching (PIM) algorithm, which dynamically allocates virtual circuits between compute and memory nodes. These virtual circuits reserve dedicated bandwidth in the PHY layer, eliminating queuing delay and Layer 2 packet processing delay at the switch while maintaining high bandwidth utilization. The FPGA testbed demonstrates ~300 ns unloaded latency for remote memory access.

title: Segue & ColorGuard: Optimizing SFI Performance and Scalability on Modern Architectures
problem: Software-based fault isolation (SFI) for WebAssembly (Wasm) incurs significant performance overhead from memory-access instrumentation and limits the number of Wasm instances that can run concurrently in a single address space due to address-space partitioning constraints.
method: Segue exploits x86-64 segment registers (FS/GS base) to encode sandbox memory bounds directly in hardware, eliminating the explicit bounds-check instrumentation instructions for most memory accesses; this removes 44.7% of Wasm overhead on a Wasm-compatible SPEC CPU 2006 subset and reduces font-rendering sandbox overhead in Firefox by 75%. ColorGuard leverages memory protection keys (MPK/memory tagging) to color each Wasm instance's memory region with a distinct tag, enabling up to 15x more concurrent Wasm instances in a single address space without requiring separate address spaces.

title: April: Accuracy-Improved Floating-Point Approximation For Neural Network Accelerators
problem: Floating-point approximation (e.g., Mitchell's logarithm) replaces expensive multiplication with simpler integer addition, but suffers from precision loss and requires careful integration into hardware accelerators.
method: April framework combines hardware-efficient down-sampling-based compensation to mitigate precision loss with a flexible bias mechanism accommodating diverse data distributions. Configurable systolic array templates optimized for NN accelerators integrate approximated FP arithmetic. Co-design framework automatically generates synthesizable arrays balancing accuracy and resource usage.

title: InfiniMind: A Learning-Optimized Large-Scale Brain-Computer Interface
problem: Deploying continual learning on NVM-assisted implanted BCI systems incurs excessive write overhead on non-volatile memory, drastically reducing NVM endurance (lifetime) and causing performance bottlenecks that make continual adaptation to non-stationary neural signals impractical.
method: InfiniMind proposes four NVM-write optimization schemes implemented in a memory controller: (1) update filtering exploits sparse and recurring nature of BCI signals to skip unnecessary writes; (2) delta buffering uses temporal locality in neural signals to accumulate deltas and batch NVM writes; (3) out-of-place flushing packs multiple sub-page updates into single page writes to reduce write amplification; and (4) waveform compression exploits structural characteristics of neural waveforms to reduce data volume. These are integrated as a memory controller layer on top of an NVM-assisted BCI system running continual learning algorithms.

title: PuDHammer: Experimental Analysis of Read Disturbance Effects of Processing-using-DRAM in Real DRAM Chips
problem: Processing-using-DRAM (PuD) operations require multiple-row activation (activating multiple DRAM rows simultaneously or in quick succession), a fundamentally different access pattern from conventional single-row activation. No prior work has characterized whether this multiple-row activation exacerbates DRAM read disturbance (RowHammer-style bitflips) compared to standard single-row activation.
method: The authors conduct an experimental characterization study (PuDHammer) using 316 real DDR4 DRAM chips from four major manufacturers. They test multiple-row activation patterns (as used by PuD bulk bitwise operations) across a sweep of operational parameters: temperature, data patterns, access patterns (simultaneous vs. sequential row activation), DRAM timing parameters, and spatial variation within chips. They measure the minimum hammer count (HC_first) required to induce the first bitflip and compare to conventional single-row RowHammer.

title: Data Cache for Intermittent Computing Systems with Non-Volatile Main Memory
problem: Energy-harvesting embedded systems with non-volatile main memory (NVM) must checkpoint frequently to cover Write After Read (WAR) data hazards, incurring both high runtime overhead and excessive NVM writes; existing data cache solutions do not integrate WAR detection and require additional hardware or software memory trackers.
method: NACHO integrates WAR dependency detection directly into the data cache controller, eliminating the need for a separate memory tracker. When a cached dirty line is read after being written by NVM (a WAR hazard), the cache itself identifies and handles the dependency without a side-channel tracking structure. This co-design reduces checkpoint frequency (because fewer WARs escape detection) and reduces NVM writes (because dirty data is buffered in the volatile cache and written to NVM only at checkpoint time or on eviction), cutting both runtime and write wear.

title: On Bit-level Reverse Engineering of Vehicular CAN Bus
problem: CAN bus reverse engineering struggles to achieve bit-level resolution of signal-to-action mappings due to massive search space over unique IDs and payload combinations. Security vulnerability assessment requires precise bit-level identification.
method: Systematic framework combining bit-level signal extraction with exhaustive mapping of control bits to car actions; validated on Tesla Model 3, Leapmotor C10/C11; demonstrated low resource consumption enabling Raspberry Pi deployment.

title: The ASPLOS 2025 / EuroSys 2025 Contest on Intra-Operator Parallelism for Distributed Deep Learning
problem: Selecting the optimal intra-operator parallelism strategy (how to partition and distribute each operation in a neural network across multiple accelerators) is a challenging combinatorial optimization problem that significantly impacts distributed training and inference performance.
method: The contest provided a benchmark suite of neural network operations and asked participants to devise algorithms that partition operators across multiple interconnected accelerators to minimize total execution time. Participants submitted model partitioning algorithms evaluated on the benchmark suite over a multi-month competition. The paper retrospectively analyzes the problem formulation, benchmark design, key algorithmic challenges (e.g., combinatorial explosion of partitioning strategies), and the quality of submitted approaches.

title: ER-DCIM: Error-Resilient Digital CIM Architecture with Run-Time MAC-Cell Error Correction
problem: Digital compute-in-memory (DCIM) macros are susceptible to SRAM cell errors under low-voltage operation (needed for high energy efficiency), but traditional SRAM error correcting codes (ECC) that correct errors in a single read-out row are incompatible with DCIM's simultaneous multi-row readout for MAC computation, leaving MAC-cell errors uncorrected.
method: ER-DCIM introduces three mechanisms: (1) a residue code-based MAC error correction scheme that detects and corrects additive errors in the MAC accumulation result in real time during DCIM computation — the first such mechanism for DCIM; (2) a progressive cell error correction mechanism that identifies and corrects underlying SRAM cell errors incrementally without stalling computation; (3) a mode switcher that repurposes redundant error-resilient logic (reserved for low-voltage protection) to boost performance in high-voltage mode, avoiding area waste.

title: Fault Escaping: Improving Robustness of DPU Enhanced Platform with Mutual Assisted VM Recovery
problem: Modern cloud servers that use DPUs to offload virtualization split VM state across the DPU SoC and the host, so a failure in either component crashes the entire machine and all hosted VMs, with no fault-tolerant mechanism designed for this split-hypervisor architecture.
method: The paper proposes fault escaping: a scheme that treats the split hypervisors on the DPU SoC and the host as redundant peers. Using hybrid synchronization, the full VM state (in a verified, consistent snapshot) is kept accessible on either the DPU or the host with minimal synchronization overhead (kilobytes of data). When one side fails, VMs migrate their state to the surviving peer and resume execution there, bypassing the failed component rather than attempting to recover it. The hybrid synchronization protocol differentiates hot and cold VM state to minimize cross-component bandwidth.

title: InstAttention: In-Storage Attention Offloading for Cost-Effective Long-Context LLM Inference
problem: Long-context LLM inference at large batch sizes generates KV caches that exceed GPU VRAM capacity; offloading KV caches to SSDs via PCIe creates a critical bandwidth bottleneck that severely limits throughput.
method: InstAttention offloads both the attention computation and KV cache storage to Computational Storage Drives (CSDs), which have high internal NAND bandwidth not limited by PCIe. A flash-aware in-storage attention engine executes the attention decode phase directly inside the CSD, with KV cache management mechanisms tailored to flash access patterns (e.g., large sequential reads). Optimized P2P transmission between GPU and CSDs eliminates unnecessary data migration back across PCIe. The system targets offline inference of a 13B model on an NVIDIA A6000 GPU.

title: Single Spike Artificial Neural Networks
problem: Standard ANNs require large-scale arithmetic with high energy consumption, while spiking neural networks (SNNs) circumvent this via biologically inspired computation but use fundamentally different algorithms from ANNs, preventing reuse of the mature ANN software stack and optimization techniques. The paper seeks an intermediate approach that achieves the energy efficiency of SNNs while remaining compatible with ANN algorithms and toolchains.
method: The design represents each ANN weight as a delay element and each activation magnitude as the arrival time of a digital signal. Complete ANNs are built on top of these temporal primitives through: (1) spatial and temporal reuse strategies enabling classical dataflows (e.g., weight-stationary) in a systolic array; (2) a noise-tolerant temporal summation operation for accumulation; (3) novel hybrid digital/temporal memory circuits for storing inter-layer activations; and (4) a temporal memory integration that manages activations between layers while preserving ANN algorithmic compatibility.

title: VISTA: Optimizing GPU Scheduling through Versatile Locality-Aware Data Sharing
problem: GPU thread scheduling typically overlooks data locality patterns across non-adjacent warps and CTAs, missing opportunities to reduce memory traffic through intelligent scheduling that exploits non-adjacent data sharing.
method: VISTA is a smart locality-aware GPU scheduler that dynamically identifies data locality patterns at CTA and warp levels at runtime, making intelligent scheduling decisions to improve data reuse and reduce unnecessary memory accesses for memory-intensive applications.

title: CRUSH: A Credit-Based Approach for Functional Unit Sharing in Dynamically Scheduled HLS
problem: Dynamically scheduled high-level synthesis (HLS) generates dataflow circuits where each compute unit is replicated per operation, wasting area when multiple operations could share a single functional unit. Existing resource sharing approaches for dynamic HLS are unsafe because handshake-based flow control can cause deadlock when units are shared without proper backpressure management.
method: CRUSH introduces a credit-based token mechanism for functional unit sharing in dynamic HLS dataflow circuits. Each shared functional unit is associated with a credit counter that tracks available slots; producers consume a credit before issuing an operation to the shared unit and regain it upon completion. This credit-based backpressure propagates through the handshake network to ensure the shared unit is never over-committed, preventing deadlock. CRUSH is integrated as a compiler transformation pass on top of the existing dynamic HLS flow.
